title: Clo Vendor Leaderboard: Connection And Partnership
description:
We’re officially debuting the CLO Vendor Leaderboard, a platform created to connect brands with the most innovative 3D-ready partners in the industry. This year, we’re spotlighting pioneers across Hong Kong and Southeast Asia: Busana Apparel Group, Cobalt Fashion, Crystal International, GMS+, Hop Lun, Newtimes Group, Daehan Global, PT. Kahatex, and Trax Intertrade.

In the fourth CLO Vendor Leaderboard video series, Connection and Partnership, hear how top vendors build deep, high-value connections with brands adopting 3D workflows through CLO and CLO-SET. Moving from physical samples to digital pipelines can be intimidating, but these real-world user stories show exactly how transparent communication, shared digital libraries, and guided onboarding change the game.

This series covers the 5 essentials of 3D success: 
1️⃣ 3D Capacity 
2️⃣ Investment & Resources 
3️⃣ Business Impact 
4️⃣ Partnership
5️⃣ Strategic Vision

markdown_content: ## Collaboration and Communication with Brands in 3D Development This section covers the importance of structured communication, alignment with brand standards, and proactive collaboration in 3D garment development. It highlights how maintaining open channels and clear expectations ensures consistency and client satisfaction. Our team stays in close contact with brands at the start of their 3D journey to ensure renders meet their expectations and are delivered in the required views and formats. Each brand’s styling guidelines are maintained as standard operating procedures (SOP) throughout development. We begin collaborations by aligning on brand standards, including standardized advantages and rendering flat takes, to ensure consistency with their virtual identity. Open communication is maintained through shared project meetings and flexible structures, allowing both sides to remain aligned on expectations and deliverables. Key stakeholders are involved early in planning to discuss workflows, required files, and integration points, building a solid foundation to meet client specifications. We emphasize proactive communication: if any design or technical details are unclear or inconsistent, we immediately contact the buyer using detailed 3D visualizations as evidence to clarify and resolve uncertainties. Our 3D team also supports buyers new to 3D by benchmarking and sharing best practices from our expertise, ensuring smooth adoption and consistent brand goals throughout the collaboration. Through disciplined rules, transparent communication, and knowledge sharing, we create harmony and produce the best results aligned with brand objectives. --- ## Structured Workflow and Visual Communication This section explains the structured process for defining and sharing 3D garment development criteria, emphasizing cloud-based collaboration and real-time feedback to streamline approvals and reduce turnaround times. We begin with a kickoff meeting defining fit expectations, fabric behavior, render style, and decision criteria. Throughout the build, work-in-progress assets are shared on the cloud with clear, real-time annotations, replacing long email threads. This approach keeps all stakeholders aligned, reduces back-and-forth communication, and avoids surprises at final delivery. One client requires all sweater samples to be created in 3D, enabling early decision-making on whether to proceed with development. Since sweater samples and edits are time-consuming, using 3D renders significantly shortens development time, streamlining the process and reducing costs. After demonstrating quality and accuracy, this client expanded their 3D library with our help, aligning with their digital transformation and growing their sweater business. We also utilize Clo’s virtual showing feature to upload new styles and seamlessly share collections with brands. Our team is trained to identify and solve issues such as pattern sizing problems using Clo’s tools. The workflow has evolved from using 3D for quick photo visualization to fabric visualization, reusable templates, and virtual approvals via Clo, transforming 3D from a design exploration tool into a primary decision-making platform. As a result, physical samples have been reduced by 30%, and style approvals that used to take weeks now happen digitally. One brand shifted 30-40% of their seasonal development into 3D, deepening the relationship as 3D became a business efficiency tool rather than just a visual aid. --- ## Onboarding Brands New to 3D Technology This section details the approach to introducing 3D workflows to brands unfamiliar with the technology, focusing on pilot projects, workshops, and gradual integration starting with less complex items. For brands new to 3D, we start with gadgets and accessories to demonstrate potential. Workshops showcase 3D sample capabilities and establish basic workflow touchpoints. Maintaining consistent communication and demonstrating early project successes builds client confidence in integrating 3D into regular development cycles. We engage brands through their best-selling ranges—items frequently repeated, recolored, or modified—highlighting practical benefits. Pilot projects emphasize key advantages such as reduced sample lead time, cost savings, and faster, more informed decisions. This approach has helped customers feel confident adopting 3D technology for long-term product development. To facilitate adoption, we start with small pilot projects producing 3D samples based on pictures or physical samples within 24 hours. These are shared with buyers with minimal effort required on the client’s part, allowing them to see results quickly and understand 3D’s capabilities. --- ## Addressing Skepticism and Building Trust in 3D Accuracy This section discusses strategies for overcoming client skepticism about 3D accuracy and adoption within internal teams, including side-by-side comparisons with physical samples and dedicated client support. Many brands are initially skeptical about the accuracy of 3D renders and their acceptance by internal teams. To reassure them, we produce physical samples alongside 3D renders and present side-by-side comparisons. This demonstrates our ability to accurately match physical samples virtually and shows our commitment to improving client efficiency. We assign a dedicated helper as a contact point for brands to address questions promptly, ensuring ease of communication. By combining sustainable, cost-saving practices with a smooth 3D sampling transition, we support brands’ long-term gains in development and fittings. --- ## Technical Onboarding and Continuous Improvement Process This section outlines the step-by-step onboarding and iterative feedback process for new brands, focusing on simplicity, clarity, and outcome-driven collaboration using Clo software. When starting with a brand new to 3D, we keep the process simple and guided. We first present a short demo using their product to immediately show value, explaining the requirements such as tech packs and fabric information. The deliverables include a 3D sample, a close-up link, and annotated paint backgrounds. After the first style, we provide a walkthrough so clients can comment and approve directly in the 3D environment. By the second or third style, brands typically gain confidence, accelerating decision-making and reducing reliance on physical samples. We avoid overwhelming clients with technical details by focusing on outcomes rather than software mechanics. Clo software is treated as an automated tool that enables strategic customization and strengthens the development framework.
